objectives: Consolidate /f/ sound recognition, decoding, encoding, comprehension, and fluency.
Measure connected-reading fluency with accuracy and appropriate pacing.
Route learners to targeted remediation when needed.
concepts: Fluency depends on accurate decoding and repeated connected reading.
A diagnostic should sample multiple related skills.

definitions.definition: Accurate, appropriately paced, and increasingly automatic reading.
An assessment used to identify current strengths and instructional needs.
A distinct skill area measured within a broader phonics outcome.

workedExamples: Sound recognition: identify /f/ in spoken words.
Fluency: reread controlled text accurately and smoothly.
commonMistakes: Treating speed as more important than accuracy.
Advancing despite a critical weak component.
Using the same item repeatedly as evidence of mastery.
Ignoring comprehension while measuring reading rate.

basic: Review each /f/ component with short controlled tasks.
conceptual: Match observed errors to the correct diagnostic component.
application: Interpret sample diagnostic results and choose a support route.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why fluency must be measured with accuracy as well as pace.
mixedReview: Combine /f/ recognition, CVC decoding, spelling, comprehension, and fluency.

mistakeBasedRevision: If fluency is low, check decoding accuracy before increasing reading speed.
weakTopicRevision: Revisit the lowest-performing component with targeted practice.

scoring.method: component-level accuracy with overall mastery gate

routingRules.atOrAboveMastery: Advance to the next consolidation/reassessment stage when overall mastery is at least 0.8 and no critical component is below target.
routingRules.belowMastery: Route to targeted remediation for the weakest component before reassessment.

outcomes: Learner receives evidence-based routing for remediation or progression.

questions.question: In “Finn has a fan,” who has the fan?
In “The fox is on the log,” where is the fox?
Which event happens first: Finn gets the fan, or Finn puts it on the mat?
options: Finn puts it on the mat

questions.question: Which word belongs to the -un family?
A learner decodes /f/ words accurately but reads a controlled passage very slowly. Which component needs support?
A learner spells /f/ CVC words accurately but confuses /f/ and /m/ when listening. Which component needs support?
Why does a consolidation diagnostic include several components?
options: It checks whether the phonics skill is secure across related abilities

questions.question: What is the best evidence of improving fluency?
options: More accurate connected reading with smoother, appropriately paced rereading

questions.question: If a learner is below the mastery target in one critical component, what should happen?
options: Route targeted remediation to that component
